as_told.title: Wooden figurines seized at Lima airport conflated with the mummies

plain: One of the three-fingered figures linked to the so-called Nazca bodies, small mummified bodies from Peru that some claim are not human, was really a knockoff souvenir, Michels says: a local journalist named Manuel Caceres made it as merchandise. Michels quotes a Peruvian forensic archaeologist named Flavio Estrada calling it "fake. It's craftsmanship constructed, built," and in a later episode he describes such wooden figurines as "confiscated at the Lima Airport in 2023," which, in his telling, is how the knockoff got mixed up with the bodies themselves.
